title: Pendulum

caveats: ball shows motion blur near lowest point when fastest
render is an animation so absolute scale is arbitrary

slow_motion.evidence: no caption, timer or visual effect indicates slow motion; swing appears continuous in real time

subjects.description: small yellow round bob on a thin black string hanging from a gray mount at top center

observation.what_happens: A yellow ball on a thin string swings side to side below a fixed mount at top center. It starts held at the right extreme and then oscillates left and right through the bottom center, continuing to swing without being caught or stopping.

calibration.note: no ruler needed: the swing is measured as an angle

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth): hold g fixed and measure the pendulum's length L in metres from its swing
reasoning: Path is a clean circular arc of ~118 deg with theta amplitude ~1.04 rad (~60 deg) and period ~2.33 s, implying L ~1.2-1.35 m with g fixed. Large amplitude means small-angle vs sin(theta) period differs, and peak amplitudes shrink slightly from 1.04 to 0.97 rad, so we compete undamped vs linear viscous vs quadratic drag to predict the held-back future.

critique.finding: It swings side to side as a long pendulum with length {L}. A little air drag with strength {gamma} slowly shrinks each swing.
critique.headline: Swinging ball fades gently but keeps steady time
critique.why_it_won: It matches the slow even fade of the swings while quadratic drag would fade fast swings too sharply.

headline: Swinging ball fades gently but keeps steady time
finding: It swings side to side as a long pendulum with length 1.2 ± 1.62e-4 m. A little air drag with strength 0.03 ± 2.91e-4 1/s slowly shrinks each swing.

eyeball.law_in_words: small-angle simple pendulum period is 2pi sqrt(L/g) with amplitude decaying exponentially as exp(-gamma*t/2) under linear viscous damping
